messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate from EU region (eu-west-1) for /v1/generate. Source: GeoDNS path. Pager: @sre-oncall. See summary: spike started ~15:12 UTC, spike correlates with increased SERVFAIL/SOA errors from Cloudflare resolver pool.

sre-oncall: oncall ack — looking. pulling logs now.

anya: I'm seeing a lot of downstream client errors with origin responding OK but gateway 502/504. Query logs from our edge show repeated SERVFAILs when resolving model hostnames via Cloudflare resolvers (eu). Route53 responses look healthy from other regions.

sam: can you paste a few dig outputs?

anya: sure — from eu-edge-3 right now:
```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 model-eu.redwood-inference.prod A
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached

$ dig +short @2606:4700:4700::1111 model-eu.redwood-inference.prod A
;; SERVFAIL
```

mike: that matches the probe results we get from our resolver health dashboard — Cloudflare resolver pool in eu-west shows ~40% fail rate for the last 5m. Route53 answers are fine. Looks like GeoDNS sometimes prefers CF for certain ISP/ASN paths and is getting noisy.

lee: quick customer impact check — metrics: EU p95 latency up 2s, errors (5xx) up 18% overall, flows to /v1/embeddings even worse. Top affected customers: AcmeCorp (heavy), ZephyrAnalytics (batch-ingesting). Not yet a full outage but significant degradation.

kat: do we have a playbook step for external resolver failures? I recall failover to route53-only for EU is approved.

sre-oncall: yes. the plan: 1) lower geo DNS TTL to 30s, 2) promote Route53 as primary for EU records (force routing away from CF), 3) monitor errors for 10m, 4) if stable, raise TTL back to 60-300s later. I'll coordinate.

mike: command snippets — Terraform approach (we'll patch via infra-runbook because change needs to be fast):
```bash
# apply quick override for geodns eu policy
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  https://infra.redwood.internal/api/geodns/override \
  -d '{"region":"eu","primary_provider":"route53","ttl":30}'
```

sre-oncall: executing now. applying override. tagging with incident id inc-1757778888.

infra-bot: Change queued: geodns override -> region=eu primary=route53 ttl=30 (change_id: ch_83422). Applying...

infra-bot: Change applied: ch_83422 complete. Propagation note: DNS TTLs respected; new clients should start hitting Route53 within TTL window.

anya: starting to see Cloudflare SERVFAILs reduce on edge probes. 5xx rate dropping.

lee: monitoring: 5xx down from +18% to +3% over 6m. p95 latency returning to baseline.

product-support: raised status: a short notice posted to the status page: "Degradation affecting EU customers — partial routing issue with external resolvers. Working on mitigation." linked support tickets for AcmeCorp & Zephyr.

sam: good. can we keep Route53 as primary for the next 2 hours while we dig into CF probe logs and contact CF support?

mike: agree. we'll keep override for 2 hours then re-evaluate. I'll also open a ticket with Cloudflare and attach resolver probe traces + ASN list.

kat: reminder — update runbook and include the exact override command + incident id for postmortem. Also collect traces from impacted customers (sampling) for SLO checks.

sre-oncall: doing handoff — I'll be on for another 30m, then @lee will take over for monitoring until the next rotation. Lee, you have the change tokens and the rollback plan is to revert override -> normal weighted geodns if errors increase.

lee: got it — taking watch. checklist: confirm infra-bot shows ch_83422 stable, monitor resolver error rate, check support tickets. If any re-escalation, I will flip back to weighted geodns and notify customers.

product-support: AcmeCorp (ticket #INC-4981) updated: we disclosed partial impact and that we routed traffic to alternate DNS provider; they acknowledged. Zephyr (#INC-4983) asked for rate-limiting mitigation while they requeue jobs — we advised to throttle from client side and we can resend webhooks.

mike: Cloudflare ticket opened (CF-98765) with probe dumps + ASN list. Requesting root cause on resolver pool instability.

anya: collecting logs for postmortem: edge resolver timeouts, CF response headers, affected ASNs. saving to inc-1757778888 bucket.

sre-oncall: closing immediate mitigation: traffic now routed via Route53 for EU, TTL at 30s, observed improvement. Leaving override active until 2 hours after start. Marking incident state: mitigation in place.

infra-bot: Scheduled task: auto-revert override ch_83422 at +2h unless a user cancels. (To cancel: POST /infra/api/geodns/override/cancel ch_83422)

lee: quick notes for handoff: keep an eye on secondary DNS latency (some ISPs prefer CF; those clients may still see old cached answers until TTL expires). If we see another spike, revert to previous policy and escalate to platform-eng.

kat: thanks all. postmortem owner: @mike. timeline owner: @anya. communications owner: @product-support.

sre-oncall: handing off to @lee — I'm logging final checks then stepping out.

lee: ack, taking over.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: inc-1757778888 -> mitigation applied (Route53 primary for EU), severity reduced to SEV2, customer impact reduced.

product-support: will push a follow-up status page update in 30m with a "mitigated" banner and note that we're investigating resolver instability with Cloudflare.

mike: postmortem notes to capture: why GeoDNS chose CF path for specific ASNs, TTL strategy sensitivity, and whether we need automatic provider failover thresholds. Also consider adding resolver health to smart-routing policy so we don't route to degraded providers.

kat: agreed — that logic would avoid manual overrides in the future. adding to backlog as a P1 infra task.

lee: leaving final note: no data loss, transient customer errors only, major customers notified. Handoff complete.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: inc-1757778888 (mitigation active, monitoring pass)."
